failure_summary.description: Answers added an implicit generic word, truncated a fixed title, gave a definition instead of the named entity, or returned an associated product rather than the requested target despite existing guidance.
A terse clue naming multiple places was resolved to a prominent travel association instead of their shared geographic or cultural attribute.

patch.reasoning: Most misses are already covered by rules about exact answer targets, minimality, and complete identifying names, so duplicating those rules is unwarranted. Add a narrow rule for terse clues that jointly name multiple places.

edits.content: When a terse clue names multiple places with a shared locative framing (such as “in A and B”), treat the places jointly and identify a common, context-supported attribute—such as their country, region, or language—if that is the implied target. Do not substitute a route, activity, or other association merely because it is prominent in retrieved passages.
